What Changed: 1.0 vs. 2.0

On the older architecture (1.0), sections only worked on the homepage. Product, collection, and other pages were fixed structures; any layout change meant briefing a developer. Apps were hard-coded into fixed positions, and adding structured data usually meant installing an extra app or writing custom code.

Shopify 2.0 changes all of that. Sections now work on every page, apps slot in as movable blocks, and metafields are built directly into the editor. This shift moved a lot of day-to-day store management away from developers and into the hands of marketing and ecommerce teams.

Sections on Every Page

This is the headline feature. Instead of homepage-only customization, merchants can now add, remove, and reorder sections across product pages, collections, and blog templates, directly in the theme editor, without touching code. For a growing brand, this means faster iteration: testing a new product page layout no longer requires a developer ticket and a wait.

JSON Templates

Behind the scenes, 2.0 introduced JSON templates, which replace the older Liquid template format for most page types. JSON templates let you build different layouts for different products or collections, rather than forcing every product into the same fixed template. If you sell both physical products and digital downloads, for example, each can now have its own tailored layout.

Metafields

Metafields let you attach custom, structured data to products, collections, or pages, things like size charts, ingredient lists, or technical specs. Before 2.0, this required a separate app or custom code. Now metafields are native to the platform and can be referenced directly in the theme, making product pages richer and easier to maintain without adding app bloat.

App Blocks

Apps can now be added, edited, or removed as blocks directly in the editor, instead of being hard-coded into your theme. This means uninstalling an app cleanly removes its code too — no more leftover “ghost code” quietly slowing down your store months after you stopped using something.

Why This Matters for a Growing Store

  • Speed: The updated architecture is built to load faster, particularly when using app blocks and metafields efficiently. Shopify’s own reference theme, Dawn, loads roughly a third faster than its predecessor.
  • Flexibility without developer dependency: Your team can make more changes directly, freeing up developer time for the work that actually needs it.
  • Cleaner long-term maintenance: Native metafields and proper app block support mean less custom code to maintain and fewer compatibility issues down the line.
  • SEO: Faster load times are a ranking factor, and Google generally rewards faster sites with better visibility.

Is Your Theme Already on 2.0?

Not every “modern-looking” theme is actually built on 2.0 architecture. The clearest sign is whether your theme editor lets you add sections to pages beyond the homepage. If it doesn’t, you’re likely still on the older architecture, even if the theme was purchased recently.

The Bottom Line

Shopify 2.0 isn’t just a technical upgrade; it changes who can make changes to your store and how much of that work depends on a developer. For a growing brand, that flexibility compounds over time.
